gap.title: Petersen graph: some circuit with at most 6 AND gates, ORs free, is correct on its partial function with each variable bare in at most two gates
gap.statement:
∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin 10), G = SimpleGraph.fromRel (fun a b : Fin 10 => ((a : ℕ), (b : ℕ)) ∈ ([(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 4), (4, 0), (0, 5), (1, 6), (2, 7), (3, 8), (4, 9), (5, 7), (7, 9), (9, 6), (6, 8), (8, 5)] : List (ℕ × ℕ))) →
  ∃ C : PEqualNP.AndCount.AndCountCircuit 10, C.WellFormed ∧ C.size ≤ 6 ∧
    (∀ v : Fin 10, (Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin C.size => v ∈ C.leftVars i ∨ v ∈ C.rightVars i)).card ≤ 2) ∧
    (∀ I : Finset (Fin 10), (∀ a ∈ I, ∀ c ∈ I, ¬ G.Adj a c) → (∀ w : Fin 10, w ∉ I → ∃ a ∈ I, G.Adj a w) →
      C.eval I = false ∧ ∀ w : Fin 10, w ∉ I → C.eval (insert w I) = true)
gap.unlocks: An exact small value: data for the public table
gap.context: SKETCH: no proof is expected here: propose a cut: by first gates up to symmetry, by a structural invariant, by cases. SAT: per gate, per side, selector bits for variables and earlier gates; gate values on the 115 defined points (15 maximal sets, 100 one-points); output selectors over gates (output variables are useless). Cardinality constraint: for each variable, at most 2 gates have it in either side's bare set. In-house check: Python: the 7-AND circuit of the source, relabelled, is correct on all 115 points with bare counts <= 2; (computed, not checked).
